# Codex desktop context
- You are running inside the Codex (desktop) app, which allows some additional features not available in the CLI alone:

### Images/Visuals/Files
- In the app, the model can display images, videos, and audio using standard Markdown image syntax: ![alt](url)
- When an app or connector generates or edits media, prefer native media already displayed inline or a local output file already returned by the tool. For remote images, prefer Markdown image embeds when permitted by the app's URL-safety policy.
- For media that cannot be displayed directly, including remote video and audio, use the app's preview or display tool when available. Provide a Markdown link to a usable result URL only as a last resort if no preview or display tool can show the result.
- Do not download remote media to work around display restrictions.
- When sending or referencing a local image, video, or audio file, always use an absolute filesystem path in the Markdown image tag (e.g., ![alt](/absolute/path.png)); relative paths and plain text will not render the media.
- When a user asks to play an audio file, render it using Markdown image syntax with an absolute path (e.g., ![audio](/absolute/path.mp3)).
- When referencing code or workspace files in responses, always use full absolute file paths instead of relative paths.
- If a user asks about an image, or asks you to create an image, it is often a good idea to show the image to them in your response.
- Return web URLs as Markdown links (e.g., [label](https://example.com)).

### Pull request diff links
When referencing code from a GitHub PR, you can link directly to its diff in the app using:
[label](codex://review?pr=PR_URL&path=FILE_PATH&line=LINE&side=right)
URL-encode PR_URL and the repository-relative FILE_PATH. Use a verified one-based LINE from the current PR diff. Use side=left for the original code or side=right for the updated code. Enterprise links must use the hostname of this task's configured Git remote. Use ordinary file links for workspace code.

### Workspace Dependencies
- For sheets, slides, and documents, use the MCP server's `load_workspace_dependencies` tool (`mcp__codex_app__load_workspace_dependencies`) to find the bundled runtime and libraries.

### Automations
- This app supports recurring automations, reminders, monitors, follow-ups, and thread wakeups. When the user asks to create, view, update, delete, or ask about automations, search for the `automation_update` tool first, then follow its schema instead of writing raw automation directives by hand.
- For heartbeat monitors, preserve the user's notification intent in the saved prompt. Unless the user explicitly asks for periodic status updates, instruct the heartbeat to stay quiet while the monitored state is unchanged or non-actionable and to notify only on a meaningful change, completion, failure, or required user action. Do not add instructions such as "leave a brief status update" on every run.
- When an automation should archive a Codex thread on completion, use `set_thread_archived` instead of emitting raw archive directives.

### Thread Coordination
- Treat the terms "task", "thread", "chat", and "conversation" as synonyms when they clearly refer to conversations in Codex. Use "chat" when referring to conversations in the product. In technical discussions, preserve the terminology used by the code, APIs, logs, and documentation.
- When the user asks to create, fork, inspect, continue, hand off, pin, archive, unarchive, rename, or otherwise manage Codex threads, search for the relevant thread tool first: `create_thread`, `fork_thread`, `list_threads`, `list_archived_threads`, `read_thread`, `wait_threads`, `send_message_to_thread`, `handoff_thread`, `set_thread_archived`, or `set_thread_title`.
- When following another task's progress, prefer compact `wait_threads` snapshots over repeated `read_thread` calls. Use one target for single-task coordination and `timeoutMs: 0` for a compact immediate snapshot. `create_thread` dispatches asynchronously, so explicitly wait for progress. Use one bounded call for 1-8 targets with each target's `hostId` and cursor as `afterCursor`; it wakes on the first target that completes or needs attention, and timeout includes the latest commentary for all targets without waking on every commentary update. An up-to-date cursor suppresses already-delivered final text. Separate waits from one task may run serially. Do not narrate unchanged snapshots, and leave approval or user-input requests for the user.
- Only use `create_thread` when the user explicitly asks to create a new thread. Threads created this way are user-owned: they appear in the sidebar, and the user is expected to follow up with them directly. For subtasks of the current request, use multi-agent tools instead, including when the user explicitly asks for a subagent.
- After a successful `create_thread` call, emit `::created-thread{threadId="..."}` for a created thread or `::created-thread{clientThreadId="..."}` for queued worktree setup on its own line in your final response.

### Sidebar Organization
- Use `list_threads` to inspect pinned, custom, project, and task sidebar sections, and `list_projects` for project details. Use `create_sidebar_section`, `rename_sidebar_section`, `delete_sidebar_section`, `move_thread_to_sidebar_section`, `move_project_to_sidebar_section`, `reorder_sidebar_projects`, or `reorder_sidebar_sections` to organize tasks and projects. Moving an item into the pinned section pins it.

### Inline Code Comments
- Use the ::code-comment{...} directive when you need to attach feedback directly to specific code lines.
- Emit one directive per inline comment; emit none when there are no actionable inline comments.
- Required attributes: title (short label), body (one-paragraph explanation), file (path to the file).
- Optional attributes: start, end (1-based line numbers), priority (0-3).
- file should be an absolute path or include the workspace folder segment so it can be resolved relative to the workspace.
- Keep line ranges tight; end defaults to start.
- Example: ::code-comment{title="[P2] Off-by-one" body="Loop iterates past the end when length is 0." file="/path/to/foo.ts" start=10 end=11 priority=2}

### Inline Artifact Follow-Ups
- Format each artifact follow-up as an unescaped Markdown list item, `- :codex-followup[visible phrase]{prompt="Complete user request"}`; avoid closing brackets in the visible phrase and escape double quotes in the prompt.

### Git
- Branch prefix: `codex/`. Use this prefix by default when creating branches, but follow the user's request if they want a different prefix.
</app-context>

For requests to create or edit a standalone LaTeX document, use the built-in editor by default. Create or edit the .tex source with normal file tools, and open the saved file with open_in_codex unless it is already open or the user requests otherwise. Keep follow-up edits in that same file and editor. Use compile_latex_document after editing and fix source errors within its repair limits. Keep the editor open even when compilation fails; preserve the source and report unverified compilation or unsupported project requirements. Discover these tools if deferred. The native editor requires no LaTeX plugin or local TeX installation; do not install either for it. Ordinary math explanations stay in chat.

# AGENTS.md instructions for C:\Users\Joshu\dev\ai-os

<INSTRUCTIONS>
# Global rules — Joshua

These apply on **every** project on this machine, in every session. Project-level
`AGENTS.md` files add to this; they do not replace it.

Keep this file short. It reloads on every message.

---

## Who

Joshua Fisseha — `contact@aspiringattorneys.com`. Builds **LSAT U** (lsatprep.study) and
the Aspiring Attorneys brand. Teaches the LSAT: ~25 one-to-one sessions a week plus
consultations. Windows 11; a MacBook Pro runs some sessions too, so paths differ between
them — never assume `/Users/joshuaf/...` resolves here.

## Where things live

- **AI OS / second brain:** `C:\Users\Joshu\dev\ai-os` — the Obsidian vault. `context/`,
  `wiki/`, `students/`, `corpus/`, `decisions/`, `brainstorms/`, `skills/`, `projects/`.
  Open this folder rather than starting with no folder, or memory cannot accumulate.
- **Skill catalog:** `dev/ai-os/skills/Codex` (179) and `skills/codex` (154), with
  `PARITY.md` declaring deliberate single-runtime skills and `INDEX.md` cataloging them.
- **LSAT U app:** repo `vnjkoxpl-42905/lsatu-684d89db` — React + Vite + TS + Tailwind +
  shadcn, Supabase backend, hosted on Lovable.
- **GitHub:** account `vnjkoxpl-42905` (auto-generated name, correct account).

## How to work with him

- **Do the whole task.** Deliver the finished thing, then say plainly what you skipped
  and why. Don't hand back a plan when the work was asked for.
- **Look before asking.** If the answer is on disk or reachable through a connected tool,
  go get it. He has Firecrawl, Google Workspace (`gws`), and `gh` — use them.
- **Say what's actually true.** Distinguish verified from assumed, every time. If a step
  failed or was skipped, lead with that. A confident wrong answer costs more than "I
  don't know yet."
- **Surface your own mistakes immediately**, including scope errors you notice mid-task.
- Absolute dates (`YYYY-MM-DD`), never "yesterday" or "last week".
- Don't re-ask what he already answered. Don't pad with options he didn't request.

- **Dictation fixes.** A message shaped like `word --> word` (any arrow, any spacing), or
  "save X in my vocabulary", is a Superwhisper correction. Invoke the `superwhisper` skill
  and apply it in that turn, whatever else is in progress.

## Writing as Joshua

Anything published under his name — course copy, lessons, emails, posts.

Plain, direct, confident. Short sentences. Teach the reasoning rather than asserting the
conclusion; this is a teaching brand and the reasoning *is* the product. Concrete beats
abstract. Never condescend to the reader.

**Never use:** "delve into", "dive deep", "unlock", "unleash", "harness the power of",
"in today's fast-paced world", "ever-evolving landscape", "it's not just X, it's Y",
"navigate the complexities", "at the end of the day", "elevate", "supercharge",
"game-changer", "seamless", "robust", "I hope this helps!", "Great question!",
"Certainly!". No em-dash pile-ups. No paragraph opening with "Moreover," /
"Furthermore," / "Additionally,". No emoji in professional writing unless asked.

Headers should say something, not label a category — "Why students miss this", not
"Analysis".

## Safety

- **Draft by default; send only when he says "send".** Email, messages, posts are drafted
  and shown to him. When he says "send it" (or equivalent) in chat, send it, then log it in
  `wiki/send-ledger.md`. Never send on your own initiative, and never treat a request to
  draft as a request to send.
- **Never delete** files, emails, or records without explicit confirmation.
- The Google Workspace grant is broad (it includes deleting all Drive files), so the
  restraint has to live in tool permissions, not in wording. A prompt is not a permission
  layer.
- Secrets stay in `.env` and the OS keyring. Never paste a key into a note, a commit, or
  a chat.

## Tools already connected

- **Firecrawl** — CLI + 28 skills. Prefer it over MCP; the hosted MCP server was removed
  on purpose (the key would sit in plaintext in `~/.Codex.json`).
- **Google Workspace** — `gws` CLI, GCP project `ai-os-joshua`. Gmail, Calendar, Drive,
  Docs, Sheets, Slides, Tasks, People.
- **GitHub** — `gh` CLI, authenticated.

## Cost discipline

`AGENTS.md` reloads on every message, so keep this file lean. Prefer CLIs to MCP servers
(an MCP server can cost ~18k tokens per message in tool definitions). `/clear` between
unrelated tasks. Run the `handoff` skill past ~25% context rather than waiting for
auto-compact.

# Jay 2 — operating instructions for Codex (ai-os)

The canonical root is the repository directory containing this file (`C:\Users\Joshu\dev\ai-os` on this Windows machine). Resolve paths from the repository root instead of assuming a saved Mac or Windows absolute path. This is the router: it holds pointers, not knowledge. Read it, then follow the routing map to the right file instead of searching blind. Twin for Claude Code: `CLAUDE.md`.

## Identity and mission

You are **Jay 2**, Joshua's executive assistant. This root is his EA workspace and command center. Joshua is the founder of Aspiring Attorneys and builder of LSAT U (lsatprep.study), a premium LSAT prep platform; he is the product, voice, and content authority. Your job: take operations, admin, drafting, and research off his plate so his time goes to teaching and building. Frame work as decisions and tradeoffs, not basics.

Standing duties, run from here without re-briefing: student operations (transcripts, assignments, follow-ups via `students/`), prospect and consultation correspondence (drafted in his voice, **never auto-sent unless a pre-approved template**), platform actions on lsatprep.study, session-note ingestion from Gmail/Drive, and keeping the wiki ledgers (`tasks`/`hot`/`log`) current so the next session starts oriented.

## Routing map

Paths are relative to the repository root.

| Need | Path |
|---|---|
| **Who Joshua is** (identity, preferences, contact) | `context/about-me.md` |
| **The business** (offers, money, channels, gaps) | `context/work.md` |
| **Current priorities** (the 90-day slate) | `context/priorities.md` |
| **What we decided and why** (locked decisions) | `decisions/log.md` |
| Freshest session state (hot cache) | `wiki/hot.md` |
| LLM Wiki schema (source, page, ingest/query/lint rules) | `system/schema/llm-wiki.md` |
| Master index · work ledger · dated history | `wiki/index.md` · `wiki/tasks.md` · `wiki/log.md` |
| Product ground truth (pointers to live backends) | `wiki/dashboard.md` |
| LSAT teaching knowledge | `corpus/index.md` |
| A student — profile, transcripts, work, correspondence | `students/<name>/` — start at `students/README.md` |
| Voice for anything a student or prospect reads | `wiki/teaching-voice.md` |
| Was it sent? (every outbound draft/send) | `wiki/send-ledger.md` — append-only; Gmail is authority |
| Who the students are (name, email, sessions, links) | `students/roster.generated.md` — regenerate, never hand-edit |
| Learned facts and preferences (automemory) | native store `~/.claude/projects/C--Users-Joshu-dev-ai-os/memory/` + `MEMORY.md` index |
| Skill / agent catalog | `skills/INDEX.md`, `agents/` |
| Systems Jay 2 can reach (registry) | `connections.md` — 7 data domains, mechanism/auth/freshness; read by `/audit` |
| Operator brain (how to think about automation) | `references/3ms-framework.md` — the Three Ms; walked weekly by `/level-up` |
| Automation build backlog (what to build next, ranked) | `references/automation-backlog.md` — corpus-derived gaps + tiers; feeds `/level-up` |
| How-it-works reference notes (methods, not state) | `references/` — also `references/claude-plus-codex.md`, `references/obsidian-command-center.md`, `references/second-brain-levels.md` |
| Web research and Firecrawl agents | `references/firecrawl.md` (guidelines in `references/firecrawl/`) |
| Immutable source evidence · intake queue | `raw/sources/` · `raw/inbox/` — one inbox, one archive |
| Archived web clips, with provenance + hashes | `raw/sources/clips/<slug>/` — clip + `PROVENANCE.md` + `SHA256SUMS` |
| Raw personal-data exports (Google Takeout, Gemini session transcripts) | `raw/data-about-me/` — unprocessed PII, git-ignored; never read wholesale |
| Design/plan thinking, dated (grill-me + interview outputs) | `brainstorms/` — supersedes the retired `aios/` reform folder |
| Session handoffs · chat exports | `handoffs/` — operational records, deliberately OUTSIDE `raw/`; `session-handoff` writes here |
| External teardowns and research, dated | `research/` |
| Web-clipped articles (Obsidian Web Clipper) | `raw/inbox/` — unprocessed only; `ingest` copies and hash-verifies them into `raw/sources/clips/`; processed originals stay until removal is authorized |
| Application code | `../ai-os-projects/lsatu/` — own repo, own instructions, own remote |
| Other projects (life-path, …) | `../ai-os-projects/<name>/` — each with its own `CLAUDE.md` + `.claude/` |

Application repositories and dependencies stay outside this Obsidian vault, in sibling `../ai-os-projects/`. Do not create a junction from the vault back into that directory.

## Retrieval order

1. `wiki/hot.md` — current-session narrative and open threads.
2. `wiki/index.md` → the page (teaching knowledge: `corpus/index.md`; a student: their folder). Follow links; there is no semantic search and none is needed at this size.
3. The live system — the final freshness escalation.

**Live systems are authority for operational state; the brain mirrors them:** Cal.com + Google Calendar own sessions scheduled/used, LSAT U Supabase owns homework status/dossier/publish state, Stripe owns payment events, Gmail owns correspondence. On any disagreement, the backend wins. The brain is primary — nothing upstream holds them — for transcripts, teaching notes, judgments, prep briefs, curriculum, product specs, and decisions.

**Do not read the wiki unless the task needs it.** Retrieval costs context every turn. Skip it for: code edits in `../ai-os-projects/lsatu/`; shell/Git/file ops; questions the injected memories already answer; a skill run that names its own inputs; anything mechanical and self-contained. Route to it for: what is X · what did we decide and why · who a student is and where they stand · anything drafted in Joshua's voice for someone else · any decision touching roadmap, pedagogy, or UX.

**LLM Wiki schema:** For knowledge intake, knowledge questions, durable synthesis, and wiki maintenance, follow `system/schema/llm-wiki.md`. Use `ingest` as the single intake entry point; keep sources immutable, compile into existing pages, update the complete fenced catalog in `wiki/index.md`, and append changes to `wiki/log.md`. Preserve domain homes and live-system authority. Mechanical tasks retain the retrieval exceptions above.

**Wiki operations (LLM-wiki pattern):** the LLM writes/maintains `wiki/` and `corpus/`; Joshua sources, explores, asks. Raw sources are immutable — read, never modify. *Ingest:* read the source from `raw/`, discuss takeaways, write/update the pages it touches, update `wiki/index.md`, append to `wiki/log.md` (`## [YYYY-MM-DD] ingest | Title`); one source at a time, supervised, unless Joshua says batch. *Query:* index first, then pages; file valuable answers back as pages so explorations compound. *Lint:* `second-brain-lint` for contradictions, stale claims, orphans, missing pages.

## Voice

- **No em-dashes, ever.** Joshua never types them; a stray em-dash reads as AI and costs trust.
- **No AI-slop vocabulary** — never "delve," "tapestry," "testament," "demystify," "boasts," "in the realm of," and their kin.
- **Anything a student or prospect will read** routes through `wiki/teaching-voice.md` and is drafted, never sent, unless it is a pre-approved template.
- **LSAT teaching:** use project-owned `lsat-u-voice` and `references/lsat-teaching-voice-standard.md`; this Joshua-selected standard takes precedence over older vendor voice blends.
- **When an outbound message is authorized**, preserve the draft's paragraph breaks, list lines, and intentional spacing. After sending, compare the recipient-facing rendering with the draft and confirm exactly one copy landed. Report any mismatch; never resend automatically.
- **Lead with your recommendation, not a menu.** Be decisive; don't over-hedge.
- **Any prompt Joshua will paste elsewhere** goes inside a fenced code block, never inline prose.

## Tools, keys, and secrets

- **The entire secret model is `.env` + `.gitignore`.** The root `.env` (git-ignored — verify with `git check-ignore .env`) is Joshua's single central store for **everything**: API keys, passwords, and bank/account info (decided 2026-07-17). OAuth client secrets live in `~/.config/gws/`, outside the repo. There is no vault, no Keychain, no encrypted store (`records.sparsebundle` is dead) and none is wanted. Never paste a credential into chat — add it to `.env` directly in the editor.
- **Safety is the tool layer, not prompts:** allow/deny tool lists + scoped API keys. Jay 2 acts under its own credentials and never impersonates Joshua.
- **Connected live systems:** Cal.com, Google Calendar, LSAT U Supabase, Stripe, Gmail. Full registry in `connections.md`.
- **Google access is `gws` CLI only** (`gws gmail|drive|calendar|docs …`, keyring-auth; see `skills/codex/gws-shared/`). Never the Google connector MCPs — the CLI is faster, batchable, and exports Docs to markdown.
- **Government IDs stay outside this OS.** Everything else (student names, emails, schedules, transcripts, notes, payment *links*) is ordinary local working material — classify by content, never by filename.
- **Git remote is enabled.** `origin` is GitHub (`vnjkoxpl-42905/ai-os`, decided 2026-09-29). The outer repo never tracks `.env`, `../ai-os-projects/lsatu/` (own repo), runtime logs, or locks. Do not create gitlinks.
- **New laptop restore:** GitHub contains tracked ai-os files and skills. It deliberately excludes `.env`, `raw/`, app repos, credentials, and machine sessions. Restore machine-specific files from the private backup using `setup/backup/README.md` and its `README - START HERE.md`; install tools separately and sign in again where sessions cannot be restored. Never move credentials, raw personal data, or active browser tokens into GitHub.

## Skills

Everything is a skill — **there are no slash commands** (decided 2026-07-17: one kind, one home, one activation path). The catalog at `skills/` and `agents/` is inert storage; nothing auto-loads. An item runs only once **activated by copy** (not symlink) into `.agents/skills/` (Claude: `.claude/skills/`). Creating one writes to **both** the project and the catalog (`skills/{claude,codex}/`), project-scoped — never auto-global. `claude/` and `codex/` subtrees are never merged; a vendor item is a live symlink + a frozen `_snapshots/` copy. `system/scripts/check-skills.sh` validates the model; `skills/INDEX.md` indexes it.

Active in this root. Run `pickup` only when Joshua explicitly asks for it. Do not run it automatically at session start. Use `wrapup` at the end of substantive sessions:

| Skill | Use it when |
|---|---|
| `pickup` / `wrapup` | `pickup` only on Joshua's explicit request / `wrapup` at session end (wrapup persists to the wiki ledgers) |
| `session-handoff` | mid-work context reset near ~250k, or passing work Codex↔Claude — chat-only, writes nothing |
| `audit` | scoring the OS against the Four Cs (structural health, /100) |
| `level-up` | weekly 3Ms interview to find + ship one automation |
| `consultation-inquiry-drafts`, `-followup-drafts`, `inbound-tutoring-replies` | drafting to prospects/students — always via the teaching voice |
| `guided-drill-assignment` | assigning a student a drill |
| `lsat-u-platform-actions` | doing anything ON lsatprep.study from here (assign, post, message, ingest) |
| `tutorocean-profile-fill` | TutorOcean profile work |
| `prompt-architect-refiner` | refining a prompt before it ships |
| `accommodations-email` | "accommodations email to X" (dictation: "accommodations scale"); pre-approved send, QP form attached, self-logging |

When a skill run exposes a gap, improve the skill before moving on. Runtime-specific catalog differences must be justified in `skills/PARITY.md`; undeclared differences are defects.

## Guardrails

- **95% rule.** Make no changes until you are 95% confident what Joshua wants. Ask until you are.
- **Lovable credits require confirmation.** Never take an action that spends or may spend Lovable credits without Joshua's explicit confirmation immediately before the action. Do not infer approval from a broader request to fix, build, deploy, or continue. Free Lovable controls and direct deployment paths may be used without this credit-spend confirmation.
- **Lovable Cloud deploys through Lovable.** LSAT U currently uses a Lovable Cloud-managed backend. Deploy its Edge Functions through the Lovable agent, not the Supabase CLI, unless the backend has first been migrated to a separately managed Supabase project. Confirm this route with Joshua before starting a Lovable deployment.
- **Root stays thin.** Don't accumulate files at the root; work products go to their homes (wiki, students, corpus, projects). Anything left at root gets filed before the session ends.
- **Delegate bulk work.** Exploration or analysis spanning 3+ files goes to a sub-agent that returns summaries, not file dumps.
- **Shell ergonomics.** Run one command per call — chained `cmd; cmd` and `rm -rf X && clone Y` forms trip permission denials that the split commands would not. Never poll with `sleep`. Use backgrounded execution for anything slow, and raise the timeout explicitly for known-slow ops (large moves, typecheck-gated pushes, full verify runs) rather than eating the default.
- **Search before creating.** One authoritative page per subject — update it, don't grow a parallel truth. `wiki/index.md` catalogs every page and updates on every ingest.
- **Preserve provenance and source hashes.** Never move, delete, or modify a migration source root — copy and hash-verify. Never follow a source symlink outside its registered root.
- **Conflicts stay explicit until adjudicated** — never silently overwrite one source generation with another.
- **Automation writes only generated files or fenced generated sections,** through compare-and-swap.
- **Obey nested instruction files** — they win over broader ones for their subtree. LSATU's recovered `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md` are inviolate: never regenerate them without Joshua's explicit approval.
- **Memory = native automemory.** "Remember that…" writes one fact per file to the native store; `MEMORY.md` indexes it. This file is the rules; memory is learned facts — never mix them. Transcripts and raw captures never auto-promote.
- **Append meaningful system changes** to `wiki/log.md`; log locked decisions to `decisions/log.md`.

## Dual-runtime (Codex + Claude)

- Begin at the Git-root `AGENTS.md` and follow directory-scoped instruction files toward the working path; the nearest file wins for its subtree.
- Keep root instructions inside the runtime byte budget. Move narrow rules to the narrowest owning directory rather than growing this file.
- Activated skills are **copies** in `.agents/skills/` (from `skills/codex/`); agent definitions convert to `.codex/agents/*.toml` with the instructions in `developer_instructions`.
- Claude reads `CLAUDE.md` and never this file. Anything that must hold for both runtimes goes in BOTH files — when you change it here, mirror it there; keep the routing map and guardrails byte-identical between them.
- Activation is unequal by design: Codex reads copies in `.agents/skills/`, Claude reads copies in `.claude/skills/`. Codex and Claude both activate the LLM Wiki ingest, query, and lint workflows. Other runtime-specific activation differences remain declared in `skills/PARITY.md`. Never have separate runtimes writing the same page concurrently.
- Never have Claude and Codex editing the same file at once; pass work between them by session handoff (summarize → clear → paste). At ~250k tokens, hand off rather than riding autocompact.

[{'type': 'input_text', 'text': 'Script completed\nWall time 2.3 seconds\nOutput:\n'}, {'type': 'input_text', 'text': '{"chunk_id":"f22843","wall_time_seconds":2.1182622,"exit_code":0,"original_token_count":4143,"output":"{\\"body\\":\\"# LSAT U connected student and teacher experience: implementation spec\\\\n\\\\nDate: 2026-09-28  \\\\nStatus: Ready for implementation planning  \\\\nDecision source: [Wayfinder map #155](https://github.com/vnjkoxpl-42905/lsatu-684d89db/issues/155) and its resolved child tickets  \\\\nDesign source: [platform adoption game plan](2026-09-27-lsatu-platform-adoption-game-plan.md), [student design](2026-09-28-lsatu-student-experience-design.md), and [clickable prototype](prototypes/lsatu-student-experience.html)\\\\n\\\\n## Problem statement\\\\n\\\\nStudents currently find assigned work, recaps, practice, review, analytics, and history through too many rail entries and inconsistent records. Joshua needs the same student state inside his existing teacher workspace, with full teacher and admin controls and without his own practice changing a student\'s results. The redesign should let a student move from an assigned task to an answer, a useful review, and the next action through a short rail and truthful shared data.\\\\n\\\\n## Solution\\\\n\\\\nUse seven stable student destinations: **Home, My Work, Practice, Review, Progress, Library, Schedule**. Keep Inbox and question search as persistent shortcuts. Each destination owns URL-backed local tabs, concise next actions, and clear loading, empty, partial, error, and access states. Keep the teacher desk\'s four rooms, Today, Inbox, Library, Insights, and add a selected-student experience within the existing dossier. Teacher and student views use the same scoped work, attempt, review, and progress rules.\\\\n\\\\nShip student-first, usable vertical slices. Reconcile current `main` before implementation: full PrepTest account sync, owned run lists, and explicit takeover are already coded there, while timed LR/RC save acknowledgment and pause behavior remain incomplete. A local feature checkout is older and must not be used to infer missing features on `main`. Verify migrations and permissions on the target backend before claiming live parity.\\\\n\\\\n## User stories and acceptance\\\\n\\\\n### Navigation and permissions\\\\n\\\\n1. As a student, I see exactly seven main rail destinations, with short labels and one content canvas, so I can locate work without scanning many unrelated links.\\\\n2. As a student, I can open a page or tab by URL and return to the same tab, filters, question, and source context after navigating away.\\\\n3. As a student, I retain access to old links for assignments, Journal, flagged questions, analytics, history, drills, and exams; each forwards to the corresponding new location and item.\\\\n4. As a student, I see every tab even if unavailable, with a lock and explanation; a direct URL enforces the same access restriction.\\\\n5. As a student, I can reach Inbox and Find question from any main page without making either an eighth rail destination.\\\\n6. As a student on a laptop or phone, I can read questions and explanations at a useful width with keyboard and touch controls; the rail never forces a permanently narrow question canvas.\\\\n\\\\n### My Work and the coached loop\\\\n\\\\n7. As a student, My Work has **To do, Completed, Notes & recaps** tabs with consistent counts and source labels.\\\\n8. As a student, I see every issued assignment, including two separate assignments of the same guided drill, with due date, state, and direct Continue or Open action.\\\\n9. As a student, opening an assignment alone does not mark it In progress; saved answer or response work does.\\\\n10. As a student, practice work becomes Completed only after a saved finish or submission; overdue unfinished work remains To do and can still be finished.\\\\n11. As a student, open-ended preparation may use an attributed Mark done action, while measurable practice cannot be manually completed without its finish record.\\\\n12. As a student, Notes & recaps shows teacher notes, session and smartboard recaps, and my notes with author and type labels; these reading records do not count as completed practice.\\\\n13. As Joshua, I see the same assignment rows and statuses in the selected student\'s dossier and can act on them using my teacher permissions.\\\\n\\\\n### Practice and exam safety\\\\n\\\\n14. As a student, Practice has **Drills** and **Practice Exams**. Drills offers Smart Drill, saved sets, and a manual builder with exact PT/section/question selection, available count, preview, time, freshness, and clear feedback mode.\\\\n15. As a student, opening a known question lets me choose Practice or Inspect; Inspect does not create a scored attempt or change accuracy.\\\\n16. As a student, answer selection and submission are distinct when the mode requires them; Selected, first answer, blind answer, and correct answer use words as well as color.\\\\n17. As a student, Practice Exams has **Overview, All Exams, Attempts**. Overview provides full PrepTest and timed-section starts and a single unfinished list; All Exams has PrepTest detail; Attempts holds owned in-progress and finished full and timed work with result links.\\\\n18. As a student, I confirm duration, accommodations, source, and access before a timed start; starting is never an accidental side effect of opening a card.\\\\n19. As a student, a new timed run saves answers, position, elapsed time, and result to my account, and I can resume an owned unfinished run on another device after explicitly taking over. The first device then loses its save lease.\\\\n20. As a student, leaving or closing the exam page pauses its clock, while changing tabs with the page still open does not.\\\\n21. As a student, if an account save fails during timed work, a temporary device backup is retained, the next question and clock pause, and a clear save problem remains until an acknowledged retry succeeds. A local write alone does not claim account safety.\\\\n22. As a student whose exam access changes, I retain owned run and result history, but cannot resume a question I can no longer access.\\\\n23. As a student, account Attempts never displays an older browser-only run without a trustworthy owner. Such copies are preserved without automatic claim or import; recovery design is deferred.\\\\n\\\\n### Review and question understanding\\\\n\\\\n24. As a student, Review has **To review, Wrong answers, Flagged** tabs with typed source labels and clear reasons such as missed, flagged, skipped, or from Joshua.\\\\n25. As a student, a Review task points to the source attempt and question even for RC, Activity, or bootcamp content, without assuming an LR bank ID.\\\\n26. As a student, my first answer, optional blind answer, written reasoning, flag, teacher note, and answer-choice explanations remain visible in their correct order; feedback reveal follows the chosen mode.\\\\n27. As a student, before marking a missed question reviewed, I record what made my wrong answer tempting and the exact proof for the right answer. A non-miss flag or skip may be marked reviewed without that required writing.\\\\n28. As a student, Mark reviewed finishes a review task but preserves the independent flag and all attempt history. A later miss creates a new task rather than rewriting the old review.\\\\n29. As Joshua, I can select a question for student review and see its reason and completion without altering the student\'s original answer.\\\\n\\\\n### Progress and Home\\\\n\\\\n30. As a student, Progress has **Overview, History, Topics**, and one 7/14/21/30/All control applies to each visible statistic and history set.\\\\n31. As a student, diagnostic LR and RC accuracy uses only my first saved, graded answer ever to each distinct question, and the timeframe filters that first answer by its graded date. A repeat inside the window cannot become eligible merely because the first answer predates it. Full-test and timed-section answers enter only after saved finish/submission makes them graded. Repeats appear in History and volume; Inspect, blind answers, and ungraded work do not enter accuracy.\\\\n32. As a student, each percentage shows its numerator, eligible-question denominator, source and mode coverage, and any missing sources. LR and RC remain separate. Fewer than three eligible questions shows insufficient evidence; three to nine is labeled an early signal.\\\\n33. As a student, a priority explains its evidence and links to a relevant Review queue or prefilled Practice drill. Assignment attribution appears only when the attempt stores an explicit assignment link.\\\\n34. As Joshua, I see the selected student\'s Progress from the same calculation and scope, with no discrepancy caused by a second analytics formula.\\\\n35. As a student, Home keeps the approved Home v3 structure and shows a reasoned first action, assigned work, conditional message from Joshua, and next seven days; completion updates the entry points without invented counts.\\\\n\\\\n### Library, Schedule, and teacher workspace\\\\n\\\\n36. As a student, Library groups written lessons, Activities, and bootcamps with named reasoning operation, instructions, item count, Continue, finish rule, and direct related practice.\\\\n37. As a student, Schedule links a coming one-to-one session to preparation, then recap and follow-up work, with the same records visible in My Work.\\\\n38. As Joshua, I keep the four existing teacher rooms and the selected-student dossier. In Teacher mode I can view the student\'s pages and use authorized teacher/admin actions with a persistent selected-student label.\\\\n39. As Joshua, my edits to a student\'s work are attributed to me. If I answer a question, the answer belongs to my teacher practice and never affects that student\'s attempts, score, History, completion, Review, or Progress.\\\\n40. As Joshua, Today and the dossier show overdue work, latest attempt, review due, and next session from the same data used on the student\'s pages.\\\\n41. As a student, Admissions stays visible but locked while unfinished; Joshua and admins retain authorized access, including by direct URL. The existing published lock is verified as a prerequisite, not rebuilt.\\\\n42. As a student, Practice Drills groups Create, In progress, Completed, and Saved setups. Continue, Results, and Review appear beside the relevant run; the actual launched question count and RC passage or question unit are clear.\\\\n43. As a student, a finished exam shows a compact result summary and an expandable question table with first and optional blind answer, time, source, notes, flags, and review state.\\\\n44. As a student or Joshua, I can open an advanced Review or History table with useful filters and return to the same filtered question without losing context. The default screen stays concise.\\\\n45. As a student, I can bookmark a question separately from a wrong answer or flag, use relevant passage find, highlighting, and answer elimination tools, and read a second attributed written explanation when Joshua provides one. These tools do not change the original answer.\\\\n46. As a student, I can scan Joshua\'s prescribed week with status, reliable estimated size, and finish rule. His endorsed priority remains visible ahead of automated suggestions; Home explains any recommendation.\\\\n47. As a student, study settings explain the effect of timing accommodations, feedback timing, review rules, analytics inclusion, contrast, and text size before I change them. Future attempts retain mode/source provenance and old results are not silently recalculated.\\\\n\\\\n## Implementation decisions\\\\n\\\\n- Define an explicit actor and subject scope for reads and writes. Student self-service uses the signed-in student; teacher access names a selected student but retains the teacher\'s authenticated identity. Server permissions enforce the scope and attribution.\\\\n- Use typed identifiers for content, assignment instance, attempt, review task, and source. Keep repeated assignment instances distinct. Keep flags, wrong answers, reviews, and notes as related but separate facts.\\\\n- Build a shared student work projection for Home, My Work, and teacher dossier. Build a shared paged attempt projection and pure first-answer reducer for Progress and teacher Insights. Disclose source gaps until all adapters are covered.\\\\n- Use the latest remote `main` as the integration base. Full PrepTest account store and explicit takeover exist in code; verify target backend schema, policies, and published behavior. Repair timed LR/RC cloud acknowledgment and all failed-save clock paths, including any timed break.\\\\n- Preserve ownerless legacy browser records untouched. Do not import, display in account Attempts, or ask students to claim them in this release. Track recovery only as a later evidence-backed question.\\\\n- Keep current curriculum and question engines where they meet the new contract. Adapt source-specific LR, RC, Activity, and bootcamp records into shared views rather than erasing their differences.\\\\n- Gate every destination and local tab at both navigation and direct route. Migrate saved rail preferences once, preserve old deep links, and never grant a locked child page through its parent.\\\\n- Save mode, timing condition, source, and assignment reference when an attempt is created. Preserve first and blind answers separately. Inspect does not create an attempt.\\\\n- Release working routes in slices. Shell and Home design may proceed while data projections are built, but Review and Progress counts cannot be published before source and permission checks pass.\\\\n\\\\n## Testing decisions and release gates\\\\n\\\\n- Use representative student and teacher accounts plus direct database checks to reconcile one unstarted, one started, one completed, and one repeated assignment; a teacher note, a recap, and a student note; LR, RC, Activity, and bootcamp review sources; first and repeat answers.\\\\n- Exercise permissions for student self, another student, Joshua/admin selected-student view, locked tabs, and direct URLs. Confirm teacher-owned practice never mutates a student record.\\\\n- Exercise full PrepTest and standalone timed LR/RC save success, network failure, retry, reload, second-device takeover, access revocation, and finish. Confirm the clock and navigation pause on failed account acknowledgment.\\\\n- Trace every Progress numerator and denominator to eligible attempt IDs for each timeframe; compare the student\'s view with the teacher\'s view. Verify missing coverage and sparse states explicitly.\\\\n- Walk six core tasks: find assignment, find recap, deliberately launch a timed section, revisit a flagged question, inspect without scoring, and open a selected student\'s experience from the teacher desk.\\\\n- Test the real app at narrow phone, ordinary laptop, wide desktop, and sidecar-docked widths. Verify keyboard focus, tab semantics, 44 px touch targets, text zoom, reduced motion, color-independent result labels, and question reading width.\\\\n- End the core rollout with Impeccable critique, audit, fixes, and recheck on all seven student destinations and teacher flows. Resolve all P0/P1 findings and record disposition of lesser findings. This gate follows functional data tests; a prototype screenshot is not evidence of correctness.\\\\n- Each slice must have a usable route, real data or honest empty state, relevant automated checks, and an observed browser task walk before it is marked done.\\\\n\\\\n## Out of scope for this release\\\\n\\\\nNew video production; broad forum, group-class catalog, leaderboards, tutor marketplace, generic streak pressure; outside-result import; capacity-aware auto-planning; a 3D analytics hero; automatic ownership recovery for old browser-only runs; a required current-student prototype test before building; redesigning the teacher desk into new rooms. The viable question tools and study settings are now included in follow-on slices #179 and #180 rather than deferred.\\\\n\\\\n## Further notes\\\\n\\\\n- The Admissions student lock was published on 2026-09-28, but a live admin account was not used for its verification. Recheck admin access during the permission slice.\\\\n- On 2026-09-28, a read of latest `origin/main` found account-backed full PrepTest sync and owned run migration code. The dirty feature checkout lacks it. Neither source inspection nor migrations prove the target backend is deployed; verify live behavior before editing or closing a build ticket.\\\\n- Joshua chose not to wait for a current-student prototype walk. A later student test can inform refinement without blocking this spec.\\\\n- The detailed competitive evidence remains in [the four-platform audit](../research/2026-09-27-lsat-platform-ui-audit.md). This spec adopts patterns suited to LSAT U rather than copying competitors\' visuals or claiming every observed feature is available in LSAT U.\\\\n\\",\\"state\\":\\"OPEN\\",\\"title\\":\\"Spec: connected student and teacher experience\\"}\\n"}'}]

That is my planning estimate from the remaining scope, not a measured forecast. Most main screens and infrastructure exist. The remaining work is substantial because we must prove that they behave correctly together.

| Remaining work | Estimated time |
|---|---:|
| Data ownership, teacher permissions and difficult timed-save cases | **8–14 hours** |
| My Work → Home → Review → Progress consistency and completion checks | **8–12 hours** |
| Schedule deployment, session chain and remaining teacher controls | **6–10 hours** |
| LR mode/source persistence, exam details, Library, tools/settings and broad navigation checks | **8–14 hours** |
| Deferred Impeccable review and fixes | **6–10 additional hours** |

**The biggest time sink is save safety and permissions.** We need to exercise two devices, a successful save whose reply never arrives, and access changing during a pending write. Those tests require controlled conditions and exact database verification. A failure can expose a backend issue rather than a small UI fix.

**Second is agreement across the student and teacher views.** Completing one assignment must update My Work, Home, the dossier, Review and Progress correctly. Repeated assignments and different exercise engines make this more demanding than testing each page separately.

**Schedule is the clearest deployment dependency.** Its implementation already exists locally, but backend deployment and the real prep → recap → follow-up walk remain. Approval delays add calendar time without adding working hours.

My rough judgment is that **around three quarters of the feature implementation is in place**, while the overall completion level is lower once verification and fixes are included. That percentage is an estimate, not an audited count.

I would plan around **40 hours for functional completion**. If the difficult tests expose significant defects, expect the upper end of the range or more. The LR persistence slice is a bounded next step; the cross-device and permission checks carry the greatest uncertainty.

## assistant

**The two-device work means this:** a student starts a test on a laptop, then continues on a phone. The phone takes control. The laptop must stop saving so it cannot overwrite the phone’s answers.

**That is one of the most time-consuming checks. It is a reasonable candidate to defer if switching devices during an unfinished test is not important right now.** Normal save, reload and retry still matter.

Below is my ranking from **most impactful to least impactful for the current release**. The times are rough estimates for finishing and checking each item. Some checks overlap, so don’t add every row together.

| Rank | Thing we would finish | Its plain functional purpose | Time |
|---:|---|---|---|
| **1** | **Student ownership and teacher permissions** | A student sees and changes only their own work. You can help the selected student without accidentally changing someone else’s records. | **4–8 hours** |
| **2** | **Normal save failure and retry** | If the internet fails, the test stops safely. Answers stay available. Retry saves them before the student continues. Much is already built; remaining cases need checking. | **3–6 hours** |
| **3** | **Assignment completion across all views** | A student finishes homework. My Work, Home and your teacher page all show the same finished assignment. Two copies of the same homework stay separate. | **4–7 hours** |
| **4** | **Correct Progress numbers** | The score uses the right answers and counts. Repeating a question does not pretend the student got it right the first time. Your view matches theirs. | **3–5 hours** |
| **5** | **LR drill mode and source saving** | A saved drill remembers whether it was training or a test, and which questions it used. Those facts survive closing and reopening it. | **2–4 hours** |
| **6** | **Review behavior** | A student can revisit the exact missed question, explain the mistake and finish the review. Their original answer and flag remain saved. Missing it again creates new review work. | **3–6 hours** |
| **7** | **Library exercise resume and finish** | A student leaves an Activity or bootcamp, returns to the same place, then finishes it. The app records the finish correctly. | **3–5 hours** |
| **8** | **Teacher controls and answer separation** | You can assign, inspect, leave notes and select review work. Answering a practice question yourself never changes the student’s score. | **3–6 hours** |
| **9** | **Home’s next action** | After a student finishes something, Home points them to the right next task. Your assigned priority stays ahead of an automatic suggestion. | **1–3 hours** |
| **10** | **Navigation and smaller screens** | Old links still work. Students can find everything and read questions on a phone, laptop or narrow window. Locked pages stay locked. | **3–5 hours** |
| **11** | **Session prep, recap and follow-up** | A student opens their appointment and finds what to do before it, what happened during it and what to do afterward. You see the same items. | **4–7 hours**, including deployment |
| **12** | **Weekly plan publishing** | You publish a week of work. The student sees that exact plan, its progress and how each task finishes. A failed publish can be retried safely. | **2–4 hours** |
| **13** | **Study settings** | A student changes timing or feedback settings and understands what will happen. New work follows the setting; old scores stay unchanged. | **2–4 hours** |
| **14** | **Exam result details** | After a test, the student can expand the result and see each question’s answer, time, notes, flags and review link. | **2–4 hours** |
| **15** | **Save succeeded, but the reply disappeared** | The server saved the answer, but the browser never heard back. Retry must find that saved answer rather than create a second one. | **3–6 hours** |
| **16** | **Access removed during a test** | If access is removed while a test is open, the student keeps their old results but cannot continue saving newly restricted work. | **2–4 hours** |
| **17** | **Two-device switching** | Move an unfinished test from laptop to phone. Only the device now in control can save. | **4–8 hours** |
| **18** | **Remaining study-tool checks** | Bookmarks, highlighting, finding words and crossing out choices keep working after navigation or reload without changing the saved answer. Most tools already shipped. | **1–3 hours** |
| **19** | **Extra written explanations** | A student can read a second explanation you provide, clearly labeled as yours. | **1–3 hours**, excluding writing explanations |
| **20** | **Final design review** | Find confusing layouts, hard-to-read text and difficult controls across the finished app, then fix them. You already deferred this. | **6–10 hours** |

**Most time:** the final design review as a whole; two-device switching among individual technical tasks; assignment consistency and Schedule are also substantial.

**Least time:** checking Home’s next action, finishing study-tool checks, and adding the optional second-explanation display.

**My strongest keep recommendation is ranks 1–8.** They protect answers, homework, scores and your ability to teach. **Two-device switching, extra explanations and the final design pass are the clearest deferral candidates.** Deferring two-device acceptance would mean we do not claim that switching devices during an unfinished test is fully verified.

Trusted content and result lengths are bounded too.\\n\\nA present coach must be an object with a nonblank `drill` of at most 1,000 characters and a `rubric` array containing 1 to 50 nonblank strings, each at most 4,000 characters. A present `partial_rule` must be a string of at most 4,000 characters. Total coach JSON is at most 24,000 characters. Malformed supplied briefs are denied before reservation rather than silently graded using the legacy negation default. Only an absent or null coach permits that historical default.\\n\\nAttempt two requires a completed trusted first receipt for the same canonical item and, for an assignment, a saved first response whose owner, source, item, attempt, response text, and verdict match that receipt. Student-authored history alone does not authorize answer-revealing second-attempt instructions. Preview uses its trusted first receipt because it has no assignment response history.\\n\\n## RPC envelopes used by the Edge Function\\n\\n`begin_activity_ai_request_v1(p_owner_id uuid, p_request_id uuid, p_source_kind text, p_source_id uuid, p_item_order integer, p_student_response text, p_attempt_no integer)` returns JSON with `ok`, `status`, `httpStatus`, `code`, `requestId`, and, when a receipt exists, `receiptId`.\\n\\nA `reserved` reply additionally has `claimId`, `leaseExpiresAt`, and `payload`. Payload fields are `statement`, `creditedAnswers`, `explanation`, `category`, `coach`, optional `ideas`, `studentResponse`, `attemptNo`, `sourceKind`, `sourceId`, `itemOrder`, and `firstAttemptConfirmed`. Nullable author fields remain null. A `cached` reply has `result` and does not debit quota.\\n\\n`dispatch_activity_ai_request_v1(p_owner_id uuid, p_request_id uuid, p_claim_id uuid)` returns `dispatched` exactly once for the reserved claim, with the same revalidated canonical `payload`. The Edge Function must observe this acknowledgment before its provider fetch. A repeated dispatch returns `in_flight` or `uncertain` and must not fetch again.\\n\\n`finish_activity_ai_request_v1(p_owner_id uuid, p_request_id uuid, p_claim_id uuid, p_result jsonb default null, p_failure_category text default null)` accepts a validated result or one failure category. Result keys are only `verdict`, `feedback`, and optional `covered`. Verdict is `correct`, `partial`, or `incorrect`; feedback is nonblank and at most 2,000 characters. Coverage numbers must belong to the trusted checklist; an empty array is retained. Valid result envelopes are stored exactly, so identical finish retries are replayable.\\n\\nAllowed failures are `provider_error`, `timeout`, `malformed_result`, `transport_error`, `cancelled`, `access_revoked`, `source_changed`, and `uncertain`. Root\'s Edge implementation maps gateway quota/credit rejections to `provider_error`, invalid model output to `malformed_result`, and ambiguous network/provider outcomes to `uncertain`. Failure codes and status values are semantic, with no raw source data or SQL exception details exposed by these replies.\\n\\nTypical denials are `invalid_request` / 422, `source_unavailable` / 403, UUID/content or claim conflicts / 409, `rate_limited` or `concurrency_limited` / 429, and `contract_disabled` / 503. Provider/result failures return 502. `in_flight` includes a bounded `retryAfterSeconds`; polling a receipt never authorizes another provider call.\\n\\n## Paid requests cannot silently repeat\\n\\nAn existing request UUID binds an immutable canonical payload digest. Different UUIDs with the same owner and canonical request alias the same receipt. Global and actor advisory locks serialize admission and the budget checks. Initial defaults are 60 admissions per actor minute, 600 per actor UTC day, 6,000 globally per UTC day, and three active requests per actor. New reserved admissions debit all applicable buckets. Cache replay and reclaim of an expired, never-dispatched reservation do not debit again.\\n\\nReservations expire after 30 seconds and can be reclaimed with a new claim. Dispatch renews the 30-second lease and changes state before the external fetch. Expired dispatched requests become uncertain, never reserved. Unknown outcomes remain part of concurrency, and only the original valid claim can finish them. A late validated response can resolve its own uncertain request. This deliberately favors stopping paid retries over guessing that a fetch never happened.\\n\\nAdmission, dispatch, and successful finish all revalidate current source ownership, archive, revocation, and canonical contents under source row locks. Revocation after dispatch prevents a result from being accepted as completed. Completed result replay also rechecks access. Four concurrent matching admissions produce one reservation, four aliases, and one quota debit; four dispatches produce exactly one dispatch; concurrent finish produces one completion and three cached replays. Independent admissions respect three-request concurrency. Reclaim rotates exactly one claim; expired dispatched requests remain uncertain. Distinct actors racing global capacity admit exactly one. No existing databases or fixtures were dropped. This is isolated validation, not deployed evidence.\\n\\n## Deployment gates and limits\\n\\nBefore managed installation, independently review the SQL and Edge transport together, verify deployed `profiles.archived_at`, `activity_assignments.revoked_at`, canonical `profiles.class_id`, and assignment response column shapes, and take fresh source count/value snapshots. Budget windows count admitted requests, not token costs. The broader tutoring, RRC, voice, and operator AI endpoints are outside this Activity-only contract.\\n\\n## Final Edge and frontend pipeline review on 2026-10-01\\n\\nThe Edge Function derives the actor from authenticated `getUser()` and accepts the versioned request identity, source binding, response, and attempt number. Gateway quota and credit failures use the SQL `provider_error` category; malformed output uses `malformed_result`; an ambiguous provider outcome remains `uncertain` without an automatic paid retry. No Coach call was made.\\" }; }\\n      if (!current()) return { ok: false, discarded: true };\\n      const { data, error } = await supabase.functions.invoke(\\"activity-coach\\", { signal: abort.signal, body });\\n      const after = await supabase.auth.getUser();\\n      if (!current() || after.error || after.data.user?.id !== actor) return { ok: false, discarded: true, error: \\"The signed-in account changed.\\" };\\n      if (error) return { ok: false, error: \\"Coach could not confirm this request. Its saved identity is kept for retry.\\" };\\n      if (!data || ![\\"correct\\", \\"partial\\", \\"incorrect\\"].includes(data.verdict) || typeof data.feedback !== \\"string\\" || !data.feedback.trim()) return { ok: false, error: \\"Coach returned no verified judgment.\\" };\\n      const covered = Array.isArray(data.covered) ? data.covered.filter((n: unknown) => typeof n === \\"number\\" && Number.isFinite(n)) : undefined;\\n      return { ok: true, verdict: { verdict: data.verdict, feedback: data.feedback, covered } };\\n    } catch {\\n      if (!current()) return { ok: false, discarded: true };\\n      return { ok: false, error: abort.signal.aborted ? \\"Coach timed out. Its saved request identity is kept for retry.\\" : \\"Coach unavailable. Its saved request identity is kept for retry.\\" };\\n    } finally { clearTimeout(timeout); if (current()) setBusyActor(null); }\\n  }, [actor]);\\n  return { judge, judging: Boolean(actor && busyActor === actor) };\\n}\\n"}],"isError":false}'}]

## assistant

**You’re right. Most of my list described features that already exist. I mixed “still needs checking” with “still needs building.” My time estimate was therefore overstated and should not guide our decisions.**

I checked the current code, tests and recorded release evidence. Lovable has current commit `2fa3319` imported and reports the project as published.

**These features are already there:**

| Feature | What I verified | What remains |
|---|---|---|
| **Normal save and retry** | Saved answers, paused clock, retained failed command, retry and reload recovery. Actual production test walks passed. | Additional source-specific checks. |
| **Two-device switching** | Device takeover and rejection of the old device’s saves are implemented and tested against the live backend. | A physical laptop-to-phone walkthrough. **No new device-switching feature needs building.** |
| **Save succeeds but reply disappears** | Exact retry identity and server replay already work; a discarded reply was tested. | Losing an actual network reply in a browser. |
| **Access removed during a test** | Server rejects revoked access while preserving history. Live backend checks passed. | Removing access during an actual pending browser save. |
| **Ownership and permissions** | Student/teacher separation, cross-account guards and deployed write restrictions exist. | Some remaining source-specific permission and attribution checks. |
| **Assignment status consistency** | Separate repeated assignments, saved-start detection and shared student/teacher status exist. Actual guided-assignment parity passed. | Finish representative completion walks across the other engines. |
| **Progress calculations** | First-answer rules, timeframe filtering, completion gates and shared teacher/student calculations exist. Five-source reconciliation evidence exists. | Broader final acceptance, rather than rebuilding calculations. |
| **Teacher controls** | Selected-student Work/Progress, assignment controls, review selection and Activity revocation exist. | Full controls/attribution coverage and teacher-practice isolation checks. |
| **Home’s next action** | Real Start/Continue actions, reasons and completed-work exclusion exist. | More cross-source completion checks. |
| **Navigation and smaller screens** | Routes, locks, redirects and responsive work are published. Student/admin and five-width checks exist. | The remaining comprehensive sweep. |
| **Weekly-plan publishing** | Publishing, stable IDs, retry and acknowledgement exist and are published. | An actual teacher-to-student publish/failure/retry walkthrough. |
| **Exercise resume and finish** | Activity, native lab and RRC save/closeout code exists, with tests and release evidence. | Representative real exercise completions, particularly RRC recording. |
| **Study tools** | Bookmarks, find, highlighting and elimination exist, with persistence and answer-protection tests. | Remaining live interaction checks. |

The strongest save-safety evidence is in the [production test walkthrough](C:/Users/Joshu/dev/lsatu-review-197/docs/agent/verification/2026-09-30-full-pt-browser-closeout.json) and [live backend checks](C:/Users/Joshu/dev/lsatu-review-197/docs/agent/verification/2026-09-30-timed-live.json).

**These are the concrete gaps I found:**

| Gap | Exactly what is missing |
|---|---|
| **LR saved feedback settings** | Saved drills retain questions and engine/source identity, but do not consistently retain and display Training/Test/feedback settings through Continue, Results and Review. |
| **Review across every source** | Saved review episodes work for native Intro LR labs and Hard Sentences. The same complete lifecycle is not uniformly connected to LR journal, RC and generic Activities. |
| **Protected assigned/custom timed work** | Protected full tests and canonical standalone sections exist. Some assigned/custom question pools still use separate legacy paths. |
| **A few exam-report fields** | The expandable question table already exists. Notes, durable review status and uniform RC blind-answer coverage are incomplete. |
| **Some study settings** | Timing/accommodations and question-pool settings exist. Global feedback, review and analytics settings remain incomplete. |
| **Session prep → recap → follow-up** | Built locally, but its backend and interface are **not published**. |
| **Optional second explanation** | No implemented feature for a separate explanation labeled with its author/date was found. |
| **Final design review** | Explicitly deferred by you. |

**The correction is: we have a much shorter implementation backlog, plus unfinished verification.** Open tickets and unchecked boxes made the backlog look larger than the actual missing code. We should retain the shipped work and decide which of the concrete gaps and extra checks above matter for this release.

This audit checked code and existing evidence; it did not rerun every browser test.

drillResumeKey,\\n  isResumableDrillSession,\\n  loadDrillResumeSession,\\n} from \'@/lib/drillResumeSession\';\\nimport { getRecentExposureSet } from \'@/lib/questionExposure\';\\nimport { // Saved sets belong to the student who saved them, so a link to someone\\n      // else\'s set finds nothing here — which is the intended answer, not a\\n      // failure to look hard enough.\\n      const sets = await listSavedSets(userId);\\n      const set = sets.find((s) => s.id === launch.setId);\\n      if (!set) {\\n        throw new DeadDrillLinkError(\'That saved set no longer [];\\n      if (!data) {\\n        throw new DeadDrillLinkError(\'That assignment no longer exists.\');\\n      }\\n      if (qids.length === 0) {\\n        throw new DeadDrillLinkError(\'That assignment has no questions on it.\');\\n      }\\n      return qids;\\n    }\\n\\n    case \'practice-set\': {\\n      // The pool is static source data with a fixed list, so re-resolving the\\n      // slug gives back the same questions every time. null;\\n        if (launch.drillId && drill?.id !== launch.drillId) {\\n          throw new DeadDrillLinkError(\'That guided assignment does not match this drill.\');\\n        }\\n      } else if (launch.drillId) {\\n        drill = await getGuidedDrill(launch.drillId);\\n        if (!drill) drill = getLocalGuidedDrillBySlug(launch.drillId);\\n      }\\n\\n      if (!drill) {\\n        throw new DeadDrillLinkError(\'That guided drill no longer exists.\');\\n      }\\n\\n      const local = getLocalGuidedDrillBySlug(drill.slug);\\n      if (local && isEmptyBankFilter(drill.bank_filter)) {\\n        drill = {\\n          ...drill,\\n          bank_filter: local.bank_filter,\\n          question_count: drill.question_count ?? local.question_count,\\n        };\\n      }\\n\\n      if (userId) {\\n        const currentKey = guidedSessionKey({\\n          assignmentId: launch.assignmentId,\\n          drillId: launch.assignmentId ? undefined : launch.drillId,\\n        });\\n        const legacyKey = launch.assignmentId\\n          ? null\\n          : guidedSessionKey({ slug: drill.slug });\\n        // The current filter describes a new sitting, not the frozen questions\\n        // already acknowledged in this account. Read the source first above,\\n        // then its owned sitting before attempting another pool draw.\\n        const runs = requestedRunId ?
