Offer an existing video as an optional explanation format if one already exists.\\n\\n## Cross-platform design for LSAT U\\n\\n**Recommended information architecture, based on Joshua\'s accepted mergers:** a seven-item student rail holds Home, My Work, Practice, Review, Progress, Library, and Schedule. My Work contains To do, Completed, Notes & recaps. Joshua confirmed on 2026-09-28 that Practice contains Drills and a distinct Practice Exams area. Practice Exams preserves its approved Overview landing with two start actions and Unfinished exams and sections, plus All Exams and Attempts. Saved sets stay with Drills. Timed start is deliberate. Review contains To review, Wrong answers, Flagged, and teacher-selected items as filters or tabs. Progress contains Overview, History, and topic detail. Library contains teaching material and activities. Source inspection after the browser audit found that the teacher already has four rooms, Today, Inbox, Library, and Insights, and Library already has Bootcamps and Activities tabs. Preserve that shell and add an obvious View student experience action. The earlier proposed replacement teacher rail of Students, Plans, Library, and Schedule is superseded by this finding. Validate the final student labels against actual routes and tasks before removing destinations.\\n\\n**One end-to-end student path to design first:** Home says what Joshua wants done next and why. My Work shows the assigned activity with time and completion state. Practice starts in a named training or test mode, with an Inspect option for a question that should not count as an attempt. The question workspace preserves first reasoning and optional blind review. Review queues the miss, flag, skip, or teacher-selected question with a reason; its checklist asks for the student\'s diagnosis before Joshua\'s written guidance. Progress shows the pattern and links to a suitable drill. A future session page ties the assigned prep to Joshua\'s recap and follow-up. This path would make the smaller navigation genuinely easier, instead of just hiding existing links.\\n\\n**Where LSAT U can be better:** Joshua can make a priority personal and explain the reasoning behind it; competitors mostly rely on automatic ranks. A recap can connect the exact teaching moment to the student\'s original attempt, next drill, and next session. Written, focused Activities can teach one reasoning operation without a video catalog. Teacher and student can share the same question identity and context rather than exchange vague PT references. These advantages depend on the shared attempt/flag/assignment coverage contract described above.\\n\\n## Updated implementation sequence\\n\\nThe detailed, source-reconciled product blueprint and release gates are in [LSAT U platform adoption game plan](../implementation-plans/2026-09-27-platform-adoption.md). Practice index | Bring resume, upcoming, completed, results, and review states together in Practice\'s Drills, Sections, and PrepTests tabs. ## assistant

**My recommendation: stop aiming for complete competitor parity. Finish a dependable LR/RC practice-and-review loop, and keep the existing teaching tools.**

These are the best cuts across the entire audit, ranked by likely time saved:

| Rank | Cut or defer | What you give up | What still works |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | **Full Review integration for every Activity and bootcamp exercise** | Every exercise would share the same review checklist and completion tracking. | Existing exercise results, saved answers, and current native-lab/Hard Sentences review. **Largest implementation saving.** |
| **2** | **Testing every possible combination repeatedly** | Certification of every source, role, screen size, and failure scenario. | Representative student/teacher flows and meaningful save, retry, ownership, and phone checks. **Largest verification saving.** |
| **3** | **The full-site design overhaul, #178** | Another comprehensive visual refinement across the entire app. | Existing design. Fix specific readability, navigation, contrast, or keyboard problems when found. |
| **4** | **Every extra analytics field and filter** | More sorting, breakdowns, classifications, and dense tables. | Original answer, result, source, time, and exact question links. Existing filters stay. |
| **5** | **Expanding the Library into a hub for every topic** | More strategy pages, worked examples, and topic dashboards. | Existing lessons, bootcamps, Activities, and the Main Conclusion pilot. |
| **6** | **Second explanations for questions** | Two different written explanations for the same question. | One good explanation and answer-choice reasoning. This also avoids substantial writing work. |
| **7** | **More training switches and preferences** | Additional modes, feedback rules, and analytics settings. | Current timing, text, repeat-question controls, and saved LR feedback settings. |
| **8** | **The Schedule prep → recap → follow-up integration** | One session page gathering all three pieces. | Booking, Schedule, My Work, and existing recaps. **Smaller saving because the implementation is already prepared.** |

**On the “two devices thing”: defer the physical laptop-plus-phone test.** Keep protection against an old browser overwriting newer answers, and verify takeover using two browser sessions. That saves setup time without removing the protection.

The clearest measured saving is dropping the RRC central-Review extension: approximately **8–16 engineering hours including acceptance checks**. Additional bootcamp families could avoid roughly **6–14 hours per distinct family**. Those are estimates, overlap with shared work, and should not be added blindly. I cannot honestly give one total saving for the entire audit yet.

**Keep these:** reliable saves, correct completion, account ownership, teacher answers staying separate, and accurate scores. Those make the app trustworthy.

Videos, forums, group-class catalogs, imports, and leaderboards are already deferred or excluded. Cancelling them again saves nothing.

**I would cut 1–7 from this release and defer 8.** No cancellations or ticket changes have been made yet.
